The corporate buyer isn't looking for 'e-waste disposal' — they're looking to resolve an event: a decommissioning, a data risk, a backlog of returns, an audit on the way. Each solution below tackles one of those events, with its own scope, process and documentation.

When the problem involves equipment and data

  • Decommissioned IT assets — Fleet refresh, end of contract and site closure — with inventory and custody.
  • Secure data sanitisation — Logical erasure with a per-device report — for leasing, reuse and donation.
  • Physical destruction of data and media — Definitive destruction with custody — for policies that rule out reuse.
  • Data centre decommissioning — From the rack to the handed-over premises, run as a project with a schedule.
  • Corporate IT disposal — The general entry point for the IT estates of organisations and institutions.
  • Documentation and traceability — Inventory, MTR, CDF and chain of custody — how the evidence is built.

When the problem is volume that keeps arriving

  • Marketplaces and e-commerce — Returns and damaged goods at scale, with a per-DC schedule and evidence per cycle.
  • Manufacturers and importers — Post-consumer, warranty and non-resalable products — with documented proof.
  • Damaged and out-of-warranty products — Brand protection and documentary backing for writing off stock.
  • Recurring collections — A continuous schedule for operations with a constant flow of waste.
  • Reverse logistics — The overview of reverse flows documented end to end.
  • Salvage goods for insurers — Salvage with photographic records, de-identification and custody.

Loose household batteries, toner and cartridges, lamps, oil, polystyrene, packaging and chemical, biological, radioactive or contaminated waste. Each page declares its scope — and every collection goes through a technical assessment before confirmation. See public evidence.

Each material has its own handling, transport and disposal requirements. Find yours in the list, see the exact scope on the dedicated page — and note that the exclusions are declared too, because honest scope avoids rework on both sides.

Technology and infrastructure

  • Electronic waste in general — The general entry point for electrical and electronic waste from organisations and households.
  • Computers and laptops — End-user IT and peripherals, with data handling where applicable.
  • Servers, racks and storage — Data centre and server room infrastructure.
  • Phones and tablets — Corporate mobile devices, with attention to media.
  • Printers — Printing equipment — without loose toner and cartridges.
  • Boards and components — Boards, components and IT scrap.
  • Telecoms — Networks, telephony and decommissioned infrastructure.
  • Cables and wires — Electrical and network cabling, assessed by volume.

Batteries, white goods and industry

  • Batteries and UPS units — Lithium, lead-acid, stationary, traction, automotive and electric-vehicle batteries.
  • White goods — White goods: fridges, freezers, washers and dryers.
  • Air conditioning — Climate control, with its own logistics and operational risks.
  • Televisions and monitors — TVs, monitors and screens of any generation.
  • Industrial machinery — Large-scale: panels, motors and decommissioned lines.
  • Hospital equipment — Only non-contaminated electronics and subject to declaration.

Loose household batteries (AA, AAA and similar), toner and cartridges, lamps, oil, polystyrene, packaging and chemical, biological, radioactive or contaminated waste. These materials require specific chains and are not part of our services. Request collection of what we collect.

Media kept 'to destroy later' is risk in storage

Every month of waiting adds data to the liability — and the blind link of transport can be worse than the wait.

Scope

Ecobraz performs logical sanitisation with a documented method and a per-media report — the equipment stays usable, and the risk is set out in writing. Data 'erased' any old way remains recoverable with a common tool.

Scope

Sanitisation is offered where technically applicable — the assessment checks the media, its condition and the requirement. Where it is not the right path, you receive the recommendation for physical destruction with the same clarity.
